thread:
linh: Heads-up — onboarding LoRA merge + int4 quant for cust-tungsten invoice parser. Quick eval pack failing on currency/decimal outputs. S3 sample: s3://redwood-evals/cust-tungsten/quickpack-1.json
arjun: Can you paste a failing example?
linh: here's snippet:
```
input: "Total: $1,234.56"
expected: "1234.56"
model: "tungsten-lora-v1+int4"
output: "1,234.00"
```
sam: hmm looks like rounding/truncation to cents — could be tokenization or a merge-scaling issue after quantization
sara: did you run with kv-cache toggled? int4 kernels sometimes shift token alignments after package changes
linh: ran with kv-cache on/off, same failure. bench-bot: quick-eval summary: accuracy 0.82 -> 0.65 after int4, MAE 12.4 -> 52.1
arjun: share the prompt/template and merge command used
linh: prompt template is standard invoice-template v3. Merge used alpha=0.75 by mistake (should be 1.0) when applying LoRA patch during the onboarding script
sam: aha — that would scale residuals down and quant exacerbate mismatch. Try remerge with alpha=1.0 and re-run quant pipeline
arjun: command we use: `python tools/merge_lora.py --base base.ckpt --lora lora.ckpt --alpha 1.0 --out merged.ckpt` then `python tools/quantize.py --in merged.ckpt --mode int4 --out merged-int4.ckpt`
linh: remerging with alpha=1.0 now
deploy-bot: build queued: quant-pack-test-84
sara: also run `python eval/trace_tokens.py --model merged-int4.ckpt --input "Total: $1,234.56"` to inspect tokenization sequence and offsets
linh: token trace shows comma tokenization changed position vs fp16 -> offset shift by +1 for numeric tokens
arjun: that offset shift is consistent with scale mismatch during merge; quantized kernels map embeddings slightly differently if residual scale is off
sam: workaround for prod: add preproc to normalize currency tokens (strip commas) for numeric fields until model is fixed, but prefer correct merge fix
linh: remerge+quant finished, running quickpack subset now
bench-bot: quick-eval v2: accuracy 0.81, MAE 13.2 — dramatically better
sara: great — alpha mismatch was the culprit. Can we add a guard in the onboarding script to assert alpha==1.0 for LoRA merges unless explicitly overridden?
arjun: yes, and add a small regression unit test in CI that quantizes and checks numeric-field MAE on a tiny sample
linh: adding test and PR, will include eval artifacts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/1324
bench-bot: saved artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/cust-tungsten/quickpack-2026-03-23/ and uploaded diff report
sara: please add a short note to onboarding checklist and the runbook about merge alpha and token-offset checks for quantized builds
linh: will update checklist and runbook. Also adding token-level regression to quickpack to catch commas/decimal shifts
sam: nice. Ping customer-success to schedule a verification run with cust-tungsten tomorrow
linh: pinging CS. Closing loop here — thanks team :thumbsup:
